content: An Associate of Science in Nursing (ASN) is an entry-level academic degree in the field of nursing, typically awarded by community colleges or similar institutions in the United States. Individuals who earn this degree are eligible to take the NCLEX-RN examination, which is required to obtain licensure as a Registered Nurse (RN). Historically, some hospital-based nursing schools that previously granted diplomas transitioned their programs to offer associate degrees. Additionally, many nursing schools that provide bachelor's degrees have developed fast-track programs. These programs are designed to allow practicing nurses who hold an associate degree to complete the requirements for a bachelor's degree in nursing within approximately two years.
